guides.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
guides.dek: Choose a format by matching it to the way you cook — not by assuming one style is universally better.
guides.meta_desc: A decision framework for air fryer format: capacity, access, counter footprint, and the shape of your usual meals. Check the retailer listing before you buy.
guides.summary: Capacity, access, and the shape of your meals matter more than the format label. Verify every model-specific detail at the retailer and maker.

guides.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
guides.dek: Measure the food and the space — not just the number printed on a product page.
guides.meta_desc: Quarts are a starting point, not an answer. A checklist for comparing air fryer capacity against real portions, basket shape, and counter space.
guides.summary: Compare usable flat area and single-layer fit against the portions you actually cook, then verify the exact model's specs on its listing.

guides.title: Cleanup and counter space: the trade-offs to assess
guides.dek: The daily friction decides whether the appliance gets used or banished.
guides.meta_desc: Questions about parts, storage, ventilation, and maintenance to check before buying an air fryer. Verify care instructions with the maker.
guides.summary: Count the parts that touch food, check the care language in the maker's manual, and measure the permanent footprint before you commit.

guides.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function appliance
guides.dek: A long mode list is only worth what the modes replace in your routine.
guides.meta_desc: How to decide which appliance modes you'll realistically use, what they replace, and how complexity fits your kitchen.
guides.summary: List the appliances a multi-cooker would genuinely retire, then check which modes have real instructions behind them, not just icons.

guides.title: What size air fryer does a family of four actually need?
guides.dek: The honest answer starts with a plate count, ends with a tape measure, and never takes a quart number at face value.
guides.meta_desc: How to size an air fryer for four people: single-layer math, drumstick density, dual baskets vs one big one, and a 10-minute measuring exercise.
guides.summary: Size by batches of single-layer servings, not headline quarts; two smaller baskets often beat one large one for weeknight portions.

guides.title: Seven things to check before you click Buy
guides.dek: A two-minute pass that catches most buyer's remorse while it's still a browser tab.
guides.meta_desc: A pre-purchase checklist for appliances: exact model, live price, returns, warranty, dimensions, recalls, and the fine print on 'dishwasher safe'.
guides.summary: Confirm the model, the live price, the return window, the warranty terms, real dimensions, a recall check, and the actual care language.

guides.title: How to use a thermometer so you never guess again
guides.dek: Where you probe matters as much as what you probe. The USDA numbers are simple; the placement is where dinner is won.
guides.meta_desc: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperatures, correct probe placement, and instant-read vs leave-in — a practical thermometer guide for home cooks.
guides.summary: Poultry 165°F; steaks, chops and roasts 145°F with a three-minute rest; ground meats 160°F — measured in the thickest part, away from bone.

guides.title: Wired, Bluetooth, WiFi: what each probe tier actually buys you
guides.dek: You're not paying for the temperature. You're paying for how far you can walk away from it.
guides.meta_desc: Instant-read vs Bluetooth vs WiFi leave-in thermometers explained, with real limits to check in maker docs before buying a smart probe.
guides.summary: Each tier buys range and attention, not accuracy. Check the probe's food-side and ambient limits, and whether an app is required.

guides.title: The first week with a new air fryer
guides.dek: Registration, a recall habit, one throwaway test, and one frozen-dinner win — in that order.
guides.meta_desc: A practical first-week checklist for a new air fryer: warranty registration, CPSC recall check, counter placement, and a first cooking test.
guides.summary: Register the product, note the model number, check recalls once at delivery, measure your clearance, and start with a forgiving frozen first cook.
